units.text: INT. SUPERMAN - CONTINUOUS
She moves towards the door.
How can you say such a thing, Mamma!
units.name: ANN

units.text: Glowing with affectionate remorse.
Oh, I wonder can you be right! Have I been inconsiderate?
units.name: ANN

units.text: She turns to Octavius, who is sitting astride his chair with his elbows on the back of it.
Putting her hand on his forehead she turns his face up suddenly.
Do you want to be treated like a grown up man? Must I call you Mr Robinson in future?
units.name: ANN

units.text: earnestly.
Oh please call me Ricky-ticky-tavy, "Mr Robinson" would hurt me cruelly.
units.name: OCTAVIUS

units.text: She laughs and pats his cheek with her finger; then comes back to Ramsden.
You know I'm beginning to think that Granny is rather a piece of impertinence. But I never dreamt of its hurting you.
units.name: OCTAVIUS

units.text: breezily, as he pats her affectionately on the back.
My dear Annie, nonsense. I insist on Granny. I won't answer to any other name than Annie's Granny.
units.name: RAMSDEN

units.text: gratefully.
You all spoil me, except Jack.
units.name: ANN

units.text: over his shoulder, from the bookcase.
I think you ought to call me Mr Tanner.
units.name: TANNER

units.text: gently.
No you don't, Jack. That's like the things you say on purpose to shock people: those who know you pay no attention to them. But, if you like, I'll call you after your famous ancestor Don Juan.
units.name: ANN

units.text: Don Juan!
units.name: RAMSDEN

units.text: innocently.
Oh, is there any harm in it? I didn't know. Then I certainly won't call you that. May I call you Jack until I can think of something else?
units.name: ANN

units.text: Oh, for Heaven's sake don't try to invent anything worse. I capitulate. I consent to Jack. I embrace Jack. Here endeth my first and last attempt to assert my authority.
units.name: TANKER

units.text: You see, Mamma, they all really like to have pet names.
units.name: ANN

units.text: Well, I think you might at least drop them until we are out of mourning.
units.name: MRS WHITEFIELD

units.text: reproachfully, stricken to the soul.
Oh, how could you remind me, mother?
units.name: ANN

units.text: She hastily leaves the room to conceal her emotion.
Of course. My fault as usual!
units.name: MRS WHITEFIELD

units.text: She follows Ann.
coming from the bockcase.
Ramsden: we're beaten--smashed--nonentitized, like her mother.
units.name: TANNER

units.text: Stuff, Sir.
units.name: RAMSDEN

units.text: He follows Mrs Whitefield out of the room.
left alone with Octavius, stares whimsically at him.
Tavy: do you want to count for something in the world?
units.name: TANNER

units.text: I want to count for something as a poet: I want to write a great play.
units.name: OCTAVIUS

units.text: With Ann as the heroine?
units.name: TANNER

units.text: Yes: I confess it.
units.name: OCTAVIUS

units.text: Take care, Tavy. The play with Ann as the heroine is all right; but if you're not very careful, by Heaven she'll marry you.
units.name: TANNER

units.text: sighing.
No such luck, Jack!
units.name: OCTAVIUS

units.text: Why, man, your head is in the lioness's mouth: you are half swallowed already--in three bites--Bite One, Ricky; Bite Two, Ticky; Bite Three, Tavy; and down you go.
units.name: TANNER

units.text: She is the same to everybody, Jack: you know her ways.
units.name: OCTAVIUS

units.text: Yes: she breaks everybody's back with the stroke of her paw; but the question is, which of us will she eat? My own opinion is that she means to eat you.
units.name: TANNER

units.text: rising, pettishly.
